title.value: Safe Option-Critic: Learning Safety in the Option-Critic Architecture
title.justification: The title succinctly conveys the focus of the paper, which is on enhancing the safety of options in the option-critic framework.
title.quote: Safe Option-Critic: Learning Safety in the Option-Critic Architecture

analysis.description: This paper introduces the Safe Option-Critic framework, a variant of the option-critic architecture aimed at enhancing the safety of reinforcement learning by learning hierarchical policies that prioritize safer decision-making. The framework integrates a regularizer that uses variance in temporal-difference errors to guide the learning process, encouraging the agent to avoid state-option pairs with high uncertainty. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated through empirical studies on grid-world tasks, continuous-state puddle-world tasks, and several games in the Arcade Learning Environment.

type.justification: The paper includes empirical studies to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Safe Option-Critic framework in various scenarios, such as grid-world, puddle-world, and Arcade Learning Environment games.
type.quote: We empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in the tabular setup.

name.justification: The paper is focused on enhancing reinforcement learning through safe hierarchical policies within the option-critic architecture.
name.quote: In this work, we mainly focus on safety from the perspective of preventing undesirable behaviour during the learning process of a reinforcement learning (RL) system.

name.justification: The paper specifically tackles the problem within the framework of hierarchical reinforcement learning, using temporal abstractions called options.
name.quote: We approach this problem in the options framework (Sutton et al., 1999; Precup, 2000), which provides an intuitive way to plan, reason, and act at multiple timescales.

name.justification: The paper is an extension of the option-critic framework by specifically addressing safety using a new objective function based on variance in return.
name.quote: Bacon et al. (2017) introduced the option-critic framework by adapting to the actor-critic model. The option-critic model facilitates an end-to-end learning of options without the need to specify sub-goals.

is_contributed.justification: While the paper extends the option-critic framework with safety constraints, the original option-critic model itself is not a new contribution.
is_contributed.quote: We modify the option-critic objective to include the negation of controllability as a regularizer.

is_executed.justification: The various empirical experiments described in the paper were executed using implementations of the option-critic model with added safety measures.
is_executed.quote: We empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in the tabular setup.

is_compared.justification: The paper includes comparisons of the performance between the enhanced safe option-critic framework and the original framework or baselines in different tasks.
is_compared.quote: It can be observed from Fig. 2a that the options with controllability (Safe-OC) have a lower standard deviation in the return.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The original paper on the option-critic model is directly referenced for explaining the basis from which the safety extensions were developed.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Bacon et al. (2017) introduced the option-critic framework by adapting to the actor-critic model.

name.justification: The paper describes experiments conducted on several games from the Arcade Learning Environment to test the effectiveness of the proposed method.
name.quote: We also show that our method is scalable to both linear and non-linear function approximation settings using the puddle-world and ALE games: Ms.Pacman, Amidar, and Q*Bert.
